name: Istanbul
tagline: Where Europe meets Asia across the Bosphorus straits.
whenBlurb: April for the tulips and gentle warmth, or September into October when the Bosphorus cools and light turns amber; avoid the crowded July-August heat and the grey, wet winter.

ourTake.lede: Give the city three nights and split them by shore, the old-city monuments on the historic peninsula, then a night or two on the Bosphorus for the modern, waterside Istanbul most visitors miss. See Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque early, then spend the afternoon on the water; a ferry or private boat up the strait tells you more about the city than any museum. Skip the Grand Bazaar's front stalls and go deep, or better, to the quieter Arasta and spice markets.
ourTake.comeIf: You want a great world city where two continents meet, Byzantine domes, the Bosphorus, and food that alone justifies the trip.
ourTake.skipIf: You want a beach or a quiet resort week; this is a city that asks to be walked and worked.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Six Senses Kocataş Mansions Istanbul

items.name: Bebek Hotel by The Stay

items.name: JW Marriott Hotel Istanbul Marmara Sea

items.name: Vakko Hotel Sumahan Bosphorus
items.description: A former raki distillery on the Asian waterfront, intimate, design-driven and right on the water.

items.name: The Bank Hotel Istanbul
items.description: A grand old bank in Karaköy, reborn as a sharp, contemporary house in the city's most creative quarter.

items.name: AJWA Sultanahmet
items.description: An Ottoman-Seljuk fantasy in the old city, richly detailed and warmly, traditionally run.

items.name: Ecole St. Pierre Hotel
items.description: A restored historic school turned intimate design hotel, in the thick of Galata.

items.name: Pera Palace Hotel
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler, best hotels in Istanbul
items.description: The Orient Express hotel of 1895, Agatha Christie's rooms and a century of Istanbul history intact.

items.name: Fairmont Quasar Istanbul
items.description: A landmark tower on a restored heritage base, polished, central and generously scaled.

items.name: Conrad Istanbul Bosphorus
items.description: A refreshed modern house above the strait, reliable, spacious and quietly capable.

items.name: Soho House Istanbul
items.description: A 19th-century Italianate palazzo turned members'-club-and-hotel, the address of the creative crowd.

items.name: The Stay Bosphorus
items.description: A slim design house on the waterfront at Ortaköy, under the shadow of the bridge.

items.name: Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Areas of Istanbul
items.description: The single building that explains Istanbul: a 6th-century Byzantine cathedral, then imperial mosque, then museum, now a working mosque again, its vast gold-flecked dome still floating over the nave. Go early to feel the scale before the crowds; the surviving Christian mosaics in the upper galleries are worth the climb.

items.name: Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Areas of Istanbul
items.description: Facing Hagia Sophia across a garden, this is the great cascade of half-domes and six minarets, its interior sheathed in more than 20,000 hand-painted Iznik tiles that give it its blue glow. Freshly restored, it remains an active mosque, dress modestly and time your visit outside prayer hours.

items.name: Topkapı Palace
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Areas of Istanbul
items.description: Home to the Ottoman sultans for nearly four centuries, a series of courtyards, tiled pavilions and treasuries that reward slow wandering. Buy the separate Harem ticket, see the Imperial Treasury and the sacred relics, and pause at the terrace above Seraglio Point for the Bosphorus view. A private guide makes the layered history land for a multi-generational family.

items.name: Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı)
items.description: Descend into a cathedral-like underground reservoir built under Justinian, 336 columns rising from dark water with the famous carved Medusa heads at the base of two of them. Restored and atmospherically lit, it is cool, hushed and short, an easy, memorable stop between the big monuments.

items.name: Süleymaniye Mosque
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Areas of Istanbul
items.description: The masterpiece of the great architect Sinan and the finest of Istanbul's imperial mosques, calmer and more crowd-free than the Blue Mosque, crowning a hill with a sweeping terrace over the Golden Horn. The tomb-garden holds Süleyman the Magnificent and his wife Roxelana; nearby lanes hide old teahouses.

items.name: Grand Bazaar (Kapalı Çarşı)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Areas of Istanbul
items.description: One of the world's oldest and largest covered markets, thousands of shops under painted vaults, each lane once dedicated to a trade: gold, carpets, ceramics, antiques, leather. For serious buyers, the discreet dealers in the old Cevahir Bedesten (the inner hall) hold the finest antique jewellery and objects; a trusted guide gets you past the tourist stalls.

items.name: Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı)
items.description: The L-shaped 17th-century market by the waterfront, piled with saffron, dried fruit, nuts, teas, lokum and pyramids of spice. Smaller and more sensory than the Grand Bazaar, pick up pistachio baklava and Turkish delight, and slip into the surrounding streets for the city's best coffee and cheese merchants.

items.name: Bosphorus by private yacht
items.description: The essential Istanbul experience: gliding the strait that divides Europe and Asia, past Ottoman waterfront mansions (yalıs), the fortresses, Dolmabahçe and Ortaköy, under the suspension bridges. A chartered yacht at golden hour, with a discreet crew and a private table, is the version a discerning family remembers.

items.name: Dolmabahçe Palace
items.description: The Ottomans' answer to Versailles on the European shore, 285 rooms of crystal, gold leaf and the world's largest Bohemian chandelier, where the empire's last sultans lived and Atatürk died. The ceremonial halls and the waterfront gardens are the highlight; go by boat for the full effect.

items.name: Chora Church / Kariye Mosque (Kariye Camii)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Areas of Istanbul
items.description: A modest exterior hiding the greatest surviving Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, luminous cycles of the life of Christ and the Virgin across every vault and dome. Out near the old land walls, it rewards the detour; recently reopened after long restoration.

items.name: Galata Tower
items.description: The 14th-century Genoese watchtower that anchors the Galata skyline; the top balcony gives a full 360° sweep across the old city, the Golden Horn and the Bosphorus. Best at sunset, book ahead to skip the line, then wander down through the steep, gallery-lined streets below.

items.name: İstiklal Avenue & Beyoğlu
items.description: The grand pedestrian spine of modern Istanbul, running from Taksim to Galata past belle-époque arcades, patisseries, bookshops and the nostalgic red tram. Duck into the side streets, Asmalımescit, Çukurcuma, Cihangir, for the antique shops, wine bars and cafés where the city's creative class actually spends its evenings.

items.name: Balat & Fener
items.description: The photogenic old Greek and Jewish quarters on the Golden Horn, rainbow terraced houses on steep lanes, antique dealers, third-wave cafés and the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate. The most atmospheric neighbourhood in the city to simply wander a morning with a camera.

items.name: Kadıköy (Asian side)
items.description: Take the ferry across for the real, unhurried Istanbul, the Kadıköy market quarter is one of the city's best food districts, dense with fishmongers, spice stalls, meze counters and meyhanes. Strong on vegetarian meze too; a food walk here beats any tourist restaurant across the water.

items.name: Istanbul Archaeological Museums
items.description: A three-museum complex just below Topkapı holding treasures like the Alexander Sarcophagus, the Ishtar Gate tiles and antiquities from across the former Ottoman lands. Uncrowded and beautifully laid out, a serious hour for anyone who wants depth beyond the mosques.

items.name: Istanbul Modern
items.description: Türkiye's leading modern and contemporary art museum, reborn in a striking Renzo Piano building on the Bosphorus waterfront with a rooftop terrace and reflecting pool. Strong Turkish collection, ambitious temporary shows and one of the best design shops in the city.

items.name: Pera Museum
items.description: An elegant private museum in a former grand hotel, best known for Osman Hamdi Bey's 'The Tortoise Trainer' and a fine collection of Orientalist painting, alongside Anatolian weights and Kütahya tiles. Manageable in size, thoughtfully curated, with a lovely café.

items.name: Sakıp Sabancı Museum
items.description: A waterfront mansion museum up the Bosphorus with world-class Ottoman calligraphy and painting, blockbuster travelling exhibitions, and gardens over the strait. Its restaurant, MSA, is a destination in itself, an easy, refined half-day for a family, paired with Emirgan Park next door.

items.name: Museum of Innocence
items.description: Nobel laureate Orhan Pamuk's novel made physical, a townhouse of vitrines filled with the everyday objects of 1970s Istanbul, from cigarette stubs to hairpins, telling a love story object by object. Quietly moving and unlike any other museum in the world; bring the book's ticket page for free entry.

items.name: Rüstem Paşa Mosque
items.description: A hidden jewel above the Spice Bazaar's warehouses, a small Sinan mosque wrapped inside and out in the most exquisite Iznik tiles in the city, tomato-red and turquoise. Easy to miss and rarely crowded; a real connoisseur's stop between the bigger sights.

items.name: Süleymaniye view & backstreets
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Areas of Istanbul
items.description: Beyond the mosque itself, the old quarter of wooden houses, ateliers and the classic çorba (bean-stew) houses is one of the last authentically Ottoman neighbourhoods, and the terrace beside the mosque is arguably the finest free viewpoint over the Golden Horn.

items.name: Kılıç Ali Paşa Hamamı
items.description: A 16th-century Sinan-built bath, meticulously restored, offering the classic marble-slab scrub-and-foam ritual in a soaring domed hall. Well-run and refined, the most tasteful introduction to the hammam for first-timers, with separate men's and women's sessions.

items.name: Çağaloğlu Hamamı
items.description: One of the last great classical Ottoman baths, built in 1741, with a guest list running from Florence Nightingale to Kaiser Wilhelm II. Grand marble interiors and a full menu of scrubs and massages, an atmospheric, historic hammam a short walk from Hagia Sophia.

items.name: Ortaköy waterfront & mosque
items.description: The little baroque mosque on the water, framed dead-on by the great suspension bridge, is one of Istanbul's signature views, especially at sunset. The square behind it is a lively weekend scene of cafés, an antiques-and-crafts market and the famous stuffed-baked-potato (kumpir) stalls.

items.name: Gülhane Park
items.description: The oldest public park in the city, the former outer gardens of Topkapı, ablaze with tulips in spring and shaded by old planes year-round. A calm green pause between the monuments, with a cliff-top tea garden looking over the Bosphorus at the far end.

items.name: Emirgan Park
items.description: A hillside grove of restored Ottoman pavilions and formal gardens up the European shore, and the heart of the city's April Tulip Festival with millions of blooms. Genuinely family-friendly and unhurried, pair it with the Sabancı Museum next door.

items.name: Galata Mevlevihanesi (Whirling Dervishes)
items.description: The city's oldest Mevlevi lodge, now a museum, where a genuine sema ceremony, the meditative whirling of the Sufi dervishes, is performed to live ney music. Small, ticketed and reverent; the real thing rather than the dinner-show imitations elsewhere.

items.name: Çiçek Pasajı & Balık Pazarı
items.description: A glass-roofed 19th-century arcade of historic meyhanes off İstiklal, spilling into the atmospheric fish market lanes behind, the classic setting for an evening of meze, grilled fish and raki with live fasıl music. Touristy but genuinely fun; the deeper backstreet meyhanes are where locals go.

items.name: Rahmi M. Koç Museum
items.description: Türkiye's great museum of industry and transport on the Golden Horn, restored trams, vintage cars, aircraft, a real submarine you can board, and hands-on exhibits. The most child- and grandchild-friendly museum in Istanbul, with a good waterside restaurant.

items.name: Çamlıca Hill & Grand Çamlıca Mosque
items.description: The highest hill on the Asian side, with the classic panorama over the whole city, the Bosphorus and the Marmara, clear enough on a good day to see the Princes' Islands. Beside it stands the vast Grand Çamlıca Mosque, the largest in Türkiye, worth seeing for sheer scale.

items.name: Pierre Loti Hill & Eyüp Sultan Mosque
items.description: Ride the little cable car up to the café named for the French novelist for one of the loveliest views down the Golden Horn, then descend to Eyüp Sultan, one of Islam's holiest sites in Türkiye and a deeply local pilgrimage quarter far from the tourist trail.

items.name: Maiden's Tower (Kız Kulesi)
items.description: The tiny islet tower marooned at the mouth of the Bosphorus, wrapped in legend and lately restored, reachable by a short boat hop from Üsküdar or Kabataş. More postcard than must-see, but the café terrace gives a rare view back at the old-city skyline from the water.

items.name: Çukurcuma antique quarter
items.description: A steep warren of streets packed with antique dealers, vintage furniture, old maps, textiles and curiosities, the place serious collectors and interior people spend an afternoon. Cluster your browsing on Faik Paşa and Çukur Cuma streets, then coffee in Cihangir up the hill.

items.name: Yıldız Park & pavilions
items.description: A wooded royal park climbing the hillside above the Bosphorus, dotted with delicate late-Ottoman kiosks and greenhouses, once the private grounds of Sultan Abdülhamid II. Quiet, green and uncrowded, a good-weather escape with tea in a historic pavilion.

items.name: Little Hagia Sophia (Küçük Ayasofya Camii)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Areas of Istanbul
items.description: A serene 6th-century Byzantine church-turned-mosque, once a model for its far larger namesake, with a beautiful two-storey colonnade and an intimate, worshipful calm. A short walk down from the Blue Mosque and blissfully free of crowds.

items.name: Hippodrome / Sultanahmet Square
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Historic Areas of Istanbul
items.description: The long public square that was the chariot-racing arena of Byzantine Constantinople, still marked by the Egyptian Obelisk, the bronze Serpent Column and the German Fountain. Walk it between Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque and the layers of two empires line up in a single open space.

items.name: Arasta Bazaar
items.description: The small, calm arcade of shops tucked behind the Blue Mosque, originally built to fund it, good-quality carpets, ceramics and textiles without the Grand Bazaar's hustle. The best place near the monuments to shop at a civilised pace; the little Mosaic Museum sits right alongside.

items.name: Great Palace Mosaic Museum
items.description: A single dazzling survival of Byzantine Constantinople, the vast floor mosaics of the vanished Great Palace of the emperors, teeming with hunting scenes and everyday life, displayed in situ. Small, extraordinary and overlooked, right off the Arasta Bazaar.

items.name: Rumeli Fortress (Rumeli Hisarı)
items.description: The dramatic mid-15th-century fortress Mehmed the Conqueror threw up in four months to strangle Byzantine Constantinople, its towers climbing straight from the Bosphorus shore. Great ramparts to explore, and the surrounding waterfront of Bebek and Rumeli Hisarı is prime café territory.

items.name: Bebek waterfront
items.description: Istanbul's most moneyed shoreline, a curve of Bosphorus bay lined with mansions, moored yachts and the city society's favourite cafés and restaurants. Come for a long, unhurried breakfast or waterside coffee and watch the city's smart set at ease.

items.name: Suna & İnan Kıraç Kadıköy / Nişantaşı shopping
items.description: Istanbul's luxury retail district, Abdi İpekçi Caddesi and its side streets carry the international houses alongside the best Turkish designers, jewellers and concept stores. The natural base for discreet, appointment-led personal shopping, with elegant cafés between.

items.name: Princes' Islands (Büyükada)
items.description: A ferry hop out to a car-free island of pine woods, Belle Époque villas and sea views, you get around on foot, bicycle or electric cart. Lunch by the harbour, wander the mansion-lined lanes, and Istanbul suddenly feels a world away; an easy, gentle day for all ages.

items.name: Bursa & Mount Uludağ
items.description: The Ottomans' first capital, reachable by fast ferry-and-road, with the tile-lined Green Mosque and Tomb, the sprawling covered bazaar (home of the original İskender kebab and Bursa silk), and a cable car up Mount Uludağ. A rich full-day for history and mountain air.

items.name: Polonezköy
items.description: A leafy village founded by 19th-century Polish émigrés in the forests north-east of the city, a rare pocket of quiet, walking trails and long country lunches of pork and homemade preserves. An unusual, restful escape from the metropolis, popular for weekend brunch.

items.name: Edirne (Selimiye Mosque)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Selimiye Mosque and its Social Complex
items.description: The former Ottoman capital near the Greek and Bulgarian borders, home to Sinan's crowning masterpiece, the Selimiye Mosque, the architect's own declared finest work, its dome engineered to rival Hagia Sophia's. A serious architectural pilgrimage for those who want the definitive Ottoman monument.

items.name: TURK Fatih Tutak
items.description: The city's sole two-star, Fatih Tutak's radical, refined reimagining of Anatolian cooking.

items.name: Mikla
items.description: Turkish ingredients through a Scandinavian lens, on a rooftop with the whole old city laid out below.

items.name: Neolokal
items.description: Heritage Anatolian dishes reborn as contemporary art, tradition, plated for today.

items.name: Nicole
items.description: French-influenced Turkish refinement in a historic Pera mansion, elegant, exacting, personal.

items.name: Araka
items.description: A garden restaurant on the upper Bosphorus where modern Turkish cooking feels both familiar and new.

items.name: Arkestra
items.description: A progressive tasting menu that ranges the globe while staying rooted in Istanbul's energy.

items.name: Sankai by Nagaya
items.description: A minimalist Japanese haven and flawless omakase, a meditative break from the city's noise.

items.name: Araf İstanbul
items.description: A pocket-sized Asian-shore kitchen doing contemporary Turkish cooking over coals, newly starred.

items.name: Alaf
items.description: Nomadic Anatolian traditions and wood-fired cooking, done with real intent.

items.name: Aman da Bravo
items.description: Refined Turkish cooking with a quiet gastronomic ambition, at a price that flatters it.

items.name: Giritli
items.description: A set-menu Cretan-Aegean seafood feast in a walled old-city garden, meze that keeps coming.

items.name: Sade Beş Denizler Mutfağı
items.description: Anatolian cooking drawn from Türkiye's five seas, regional dishes rarely seen on a city menu.

items.name: Aheste
items.description: Small plates of modern Turkish with a lightness of touch, a Pera favourite.

items.name: Cuma
items.description: A relaxed all-day room in antique-lined Çukurcuma, Mediterranean-Turkish cooking, done simply and well.

items.name: Karaköy Lokantası
items.description: A beloved tiled meyhane serving the classics of Istanbul cooking, meze by day, raki tables by night.

items.name: Tersane
items.description: Traditional meze and charcoal-grilled meats in the old shipyard quarter, honest and full-flavoured.

items.name: Pandeli
items.description: A turquoise-tiled institution above the Spice Bazaar, serving Ottoman classics since 1901.

items.name: Calipso
items.description: Meze and Aegean seafood on the Anatolian side, a locals' favourite worth the crossing.

items.name: Çırağan Palace Kempinski, Bosphorus terrace bar
credentials: Genuine standing, Çırağan Palace Kempinski (Forbes Travel Guide Five-Star; The Leading Hotels of the World)
items.description: A drink on the terrace of a restored imperial palace, the Bosphorus lit and moving at your feet, the city's grandest nightcap.

items.name: Pera Palace, Orient Bar
credentials: Genuine standing, Pera Palace Hotel (Condé Nast Traveler, best hotels in Istanbul)
items.description: A cocktail inside the 1895 Orient Express hotel, Agatha Christie's Istanbul, in wood, brass and low light.

items.name: Alexandra Cocktail Bar
credentials: Genuine standing, Osman Fethi Baycan, The World's 50 Best Bars Academy (Türkiye)
items.description: A historic Bosphorus house turned serious cocktail address, with a rooftop over the strait and a bartender in the 50 Best Bars Academy.

items.name: Fahri Konsolos
credentials: The World's 50 Best, '50 Hours in Istanbul' (Discovery editorial)
items.description: The Asian shore's most inventive bar, house liquors, bitters and infusions built on Anatolian ingredients like sumac and pomegranate molasses.

items.name: Mikla (rooftop bar)
credentials: The World's 50 Best, '50 Hours in Istanbul' (Discovery editorial)
items.description: Sunset drinks above the whole old city, atop the Marmara Pera, the rooftop attached to one of Istanbul's great restaurants.

items.name: Bebek Hotel rooftop bar
credentials: The World's 50 Best, '50 Hours in Istanbul' (Discovery editorial)
items.description: A mid-century landmark on the Bebek waterfront, cocktails at the water's edge in the city's most fashionable village.

items.name: 360 Istanbul
credentials: Genuine standing, Istanbul's original and best-known Beyoğlu rooftop
items.description: The rooftop that named the genre, a full 360° sweep of Bosphorus, Golden Horn and Sultanahmet from one terrace.

items.name: Asmalı Cavit
credentials: The World's 50 Best, '50 Hours in Istanbul' (Discovery editorial)
items.description: The meyhane other meyhanes are measured against, rakı, meze and long tables where strangers become regulars.

items.name: Muuto
credentials: The World's 50 Best, '50 Hours in Istanbul' (Discovery editorial)
items.description: Chef Umut Karakuş's Anatolian small-plates bar, colourful meze made for sharing over a long, loud table.

plan.heading: 4 days in Istanbul, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Enter Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque at opening, then the Basilica Cistern while it is still calm.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Topkapı Palace and its harem, followed by a slow lunch of mezes in a Sultanahmet courtyard.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Mikla, Mehmet Gürs's rooftop table looking across the Golden Horn, and a Bosphorus view over rakı.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Grand Bazaar with a guide who knows the good carpet and gold dealers, then the Spice Bazaar.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A private morning-to-afternoon boat up the Bosphorus, pausing at Ortaköy and the Rumeli fortress.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Fish and meze on the water at a Kılıç family table, or the refined Turkish tasting at Neolokal.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Istanbul Modern in its new Renzo Piano building, then coffee in the galleries of Karaköy.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A traditional scrub and rest at the restored Kılıç Ali Paşa Hammam.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Turk Fatih Tutak, the city's two-star kitchen, reworking Anatolian cooking.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Cross to Kadıköy and walk its produce market and coffee roasters with a local.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Çamlıca Hill for the panorama, then tea in a Beylerbeyi garden by the water.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A last dinner back on the European shore at the Shangri-La or Six Senses Kocataş Mansions terrace.

items.name: Sultanahmet
items.description: The historic peninsula with Hagia Sophia and the palaces at your feet, convenient for sightseeing, quiet at night, but touristy.

items.name: Beyoğlu (Karaköy & Galata)
items.description: The lively modern side, galleries, rooftop bars and restaurants around the Galata Tower; for those who want the city's pulse.

items.name: Bosphorus shore (Beşiktaş to Bebek)
items.description: Waterside luxury hotels and yalı living along the strait; suits travellers who want views, calm and boat access.

events.name: Istanbul Tulip Festival
events.note: Millions of tulips planted across Emirgan Park and the city's squares, honouring the flower's Ottoman origins.

events.name: Istanbul Music Festival
events.note: Turkey's leading classical festival, staging concerts in historic venues from Hagia Irene to Bosphorus palaces.

events.name: Istanbul Jazz Festival
events.note: Jazz, soul and world music across the city's iconic stages, from parks to waterfront terraces.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Stay on the European side, Beşiktaş, Nişantaşı, or a Bosphorus-front hotel; dress is cosmopolitan but modest shoulders and knees are needed to enter mosques, where shoes come off.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Istanbul Airport (IST) on the European side; a private car handles the 45–60 minute transfer, or a hotel-arranged helicopter or Bosphorus boat for those staying waterside.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private driver with a local guide is essential given traffic and the two continents; the old city (Sultanahmet) is best on foot, and a private boat is the elegant way to cross the Bosphorus.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: eSIM works well; note Turkey registers phone IMEIs, so a stay beyond a few weeks on a local SIM can trigger a block, eSIM avoids this.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: The Turkish lira (TRY) is the currency; cards are widely taken, carry some cash for the bazaars, and rounding up or 10% is the tipping norm.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: April-May and September-October are ideal, mild, dry, the Bosphorus luminous; July-August is hot and packed, and December-February is cold, wet and grey.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Direct from Delhi and Mumbai on Turkish Airlines (about 7 hours) with an excellent Dreamliner business cabin; IndiGo also flies it nonstop. Istanbul Airport is Turkish's home hub, the flagship business lounge is exceptional if you're connecting onward.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No special vaccinations beyond routine; be current on hepatitis A and typhoid. Tap water is best avoided for drinking, stick to bottled. Safe overall; usual care against pickpockets and touts around the Grand Bazaar and Sultanahmet.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Very easy for vegetarians, meze culture, fresh produce, breads and mezze are largely veg. Jain needs briefing (onion/garlic are pervasive). Indian food is easy to find; for excellent vegetarian Turkish, Çiya Sofrası in Kadıköy is a standout.
